doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: Why musicians got into drugs and trouble
summary: Bucky explains big bands got into trouble on days off when dealers waited for them.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: This may be an obvious question by why during the 40s and 50s especially, musicians, especially jazz musicians, had that reputation you know. They either drank or they were doing drugs or whatever. Why? Why did they do it or why was it —

I don’t know. Every time a big band had a day off they all got into trouble. Because all the junkies would come and serve them for nothing. You know what I mean? And that’s why a lot of big bands, a lot of those guys died early. That’s my conception.
Because there was people out there waiting —
Yeah, waiting for you to show up. When you were working you couldn’t get in trouble, you had to play.
When you had a day off, forget it.
